how_to_read: sentences[].w = first..last word id inside this chapter; word k (0-based) of the sentence is first+k and `ar` is the spoken text (its space-separated tokens are those words); fr = [start_frame, end_frame] at 24 fps from the word map; impact = hook words (id=text); num = spoken numbers with data-contract fact ids; first_mention = glossary terms to chip (id=term); dup = same claim in another chapter. Anchor with {word, lead_frames} only. Visual candidates are ideas, never footage.

constraints.anchors: {word, lead_frames} only; never seconds or frames; event frame = word start - lead_frames
constraints.lead_frames: kinetic word -3, graphic state change -2, shot cut -4..-6 (inside a pause >= 200 ms), counter starts at the number word
constraints.density: >= 20 events/min; no gap > 4 s without an event (hold <= 6 s with reason); shot median 6-12 s, max 25 s (shots > 12 s: an event every 3 s)
constraints.coverage: every sentence >= 1 anchored event; >= 80 % of sentences a mechanism event; every spoken number and every first-mention term on screen
constraints.kinetic: 8-20 kinetic words per minute; <= 6 words and <= 2 lines on screen; impact word 1-2 words
constraints.fx: hero (real-time 3D) <= 5 % of chapter frames (ADR-002 RT5); fx_tier lite|standard|hero
constraints.text: text on busy backgrounds needs a plate or halo; sizes and safe areas: 04 sections 3.2 and 3.4
banned: invented numbers (every number: data-contract id or source sentence)
constraints.components: use only frozen components (harness/schemas/components/); requests go to corpus/specs/_component_requests.jsonl
constraints.chapter_rhythm: problem -> mental model -> progressive visual -> worked example -> prediction -> failure (crit) -> fix (ok) -> callback -> artifact (per chapter, not per sentence)

storyboard_notes.text: CH-15..CH-20 zigzag and CH-17 before CH-23 (ADR-001): open and close with callbacks that re-establish where we are on the A-01 map and name the chapter we return to.

sentences.ar: الـalgorithms أسهل إنك تحسّها من إنك تحفظها، بشرط إنك تعدّ العمليات على الشاشة بدل ما تكتب جدول في الآخر.
sentences.en: Algorithms are easier to feel than to memorise, provided you count the operations on screen instead of writing a table at the end.

sentences.ar: الـlinear search بيقرا لحد ما يلاقي؛ والـbinary search بينصّف المساحة كل مرة.
sentences.en: Linear search reads until it finds; binary search halves the space each time.

sentences.ar: على ستاشر عنصر دي حاجة ما تفرقش.
sentences.en: On sixteen items that is a shrug.

sentences.ar: على مليون عنصر دي الفرق بين صفحة بتفتح وصفحة لأ.
sentences.en: On a million items it is the difference between a page that loads and a page that does not.

sentences.ar: والـhash table بتدّيك lookup بزمن ثابت في المتوسط، وكلمة في المتوسط دي شغّالة بجد:
sentences.en: A hash table gives you constant-time lookup on average, and that phrase on average is doing real work:

sentences.ar: الـcollisions مش حالة استثنائية، دي الحالة العادية، والـload factor هو الرقم اللي بيحدد إمتى الجدول كله لازم يتبني من أول وجديد.
sentences.en: Collisions are not an edge case, they are the normal case, and the load factor is the number that decides when the whole table has to be rebuilt.

sentences.ar: ودلوقتي الجملة اللي تستاهل تاخدها من الشابتر ده: الـcontainer هو اللي بيعرّف الـalgorithm.
sentences.en: Now the sentence worth taking away from this chapter: the container defines the algorithm.

sentences.ar: الـBFS عبارة عن queue، فبيستكشف مستوى بمستوى وبيلاقي أقل عدد خطوات.
sentences.en: Breadth-first search is a queue, so it explores level by level and finds the fewest hops.
Depth-first search is a stack, so it dives.

sentences.ar: وDijkstra عبارة عن priority queue، فبيوسّع دايماً أرخص node في الجبهة ويلاقي أرخص طريق تلتاشر هنا.
sentences.en: Dijkstra is a priority queue, so it always expands the cheapest frontier node and finds the cheapest path — thirteen, here.

sentences.ar: بصّ على الـfrontier والـvisited جنب الـgraph والسلوك يبطل يبقى حاجة تتحفظ.
sentences.en: Watch the frontier and the visited set beside the graph and the behaviour stops being something to remember.

sentences.ar: وده مهم أبعد بكتير من الـinterviews: الـtopological sort على directed acyclic graph هو بالظبط إزاي الـorchestrator بيقرر إيه اللي ينفع يشتغل بعد كده.
sentences.en: And this matters far beyond interviews: a topological sort over a directed acyclic graph is exactly how an orchestrator decides what may run next.

sentences.ar: ضيف edge واحدة تقفل دورة، والجدول كله يبقى مستحيل وده بالظبط الـerror اللي Airflow هتدّيهولك بعد كام شابتر من دلوقتي.
sentences.en: Add one edge that closes a cycle and the whole schedule becomes impossible — which is precisely the error Airflow gives you, a few chapters from now.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

referenced.ctx: - Linear search over 16 sorted items: up to 16 comparisons;
- Linear search over 16 sorted items: up to 16 comparisons;
Dijkstra's shortest path on the demo graph costs 13.
Training error at k = 1 is zero by construction — which is why leave-one-out error is shown beside it.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.
glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: Base-two representation using only 0 and 1, the form in which computers store all data an…
concepts.failure: Reading binary digits as decimal, forgetting each place is a power of two.

concepts.def_en: A structure that maps keys to values through a hash function, giving constant-time lookup on average.
concepts.def_ar: بنية بتربط الـkeys بالـvalues عن طريق hash function، وبتدّي lookup بزمن ثابت في المتوسط.
concepts.failure: Assuming lookup is always constant time, ignoring collisions that slow it down.

concepts.def_en: Data organized into rows and columns under a fixed structure; the basic building block of…
concepts.failure: Treating a table like a spreadsheet: mixed meanings, merged cells and no keys.

concepts.def_en: The ratio of stored items to buckets in a hash table; as it grows, collisions rise and the table must be rebuilt.
concepts.def_ar: نسبة امتلاء الـhash table: عدد العناصر على عدد الـbuckets؛ لما تعلى الـcollisions بتزيد والجدول لازم يتبني من جديد.
concepts.failure: Letting the load factor climb unchecked, so collisions pile up and lookups degrade.

concepts.def_en: A running, isolated instance of an image, packaging an app with its dependencies so it behaves the same on any host.
concepts.def_ar: نسخة شغالة ومعزولة من الـimage، بتغلّف التطبيق مع الـdependencies بتاعته فيشتغل بنفس الطريقة على أي host.
concepts.failure: Storing important data inside the container's writable layer; it disappears when the container is removed.

concepts.def_en: Breadth-first search explores a graph level by level using a queue, so it finds paths with the fewest hops.
concepts.def_ar: بحث بالعرض: بيستكشف الـgraph مستوى مستوى باستخدام queue، فبيلاقي الطريق بأقل عدد hops.
concepts.failure: Swapping the queue for a stack silently turns it into depth-first search.

concepts.def_en: A first-in, first-out collection: items are added at the back and removed from the front.
concepts.failure: Confusing FIFO queues with LIFO stacks, which changes the traversal order entirely.

concepts.def_en: Depth-first search follows one path as deep as possible before backing up, using a stack instead of a queue.
concepts.def_ar: بحث بالعمق: بيمشي في مسار واحد لأعمق نقطة قبل ما يرجع، وبيستخدم stack بدل الـqueue.
concepts.failure: Expecting DFS to return the shortest path; it dives and may find a longer one.

concepts.def_en: Last-in, first-out structure; in memory, the call stack where function frames are pushed…
concepts.failure: Mixing up stack and heap, or recursing too deeply until the stack overflows.

concepts.def_en: A set of nodes connected by edges, used to model relationships such as roads, dependencie…
concepts.failure: Confusing a graph (nodes and edges) with a chart (plotted data).

concepts.def_en: Ordering the nodes of a DAG so every task comes after all the tasks it depends on.
concepts.def_ar: ترتيب لـnodes الـDAG بحيث كل task تيجي بعد كل الـtasks اللي معتمدة عليها.
concepts.failure: Running it on a graph with a cycle, where no valid order exists.

concepts.def_en: A graph whose edges have direction and no cycles, used to model task dependencies so work…
concepts.failure: A dependency loop creates a cycle, so no valid run order exists.

concepts.def_en: A message or failure signalling that something went wrong; read it first, since it usuall…
concepts.failure: Pasting the error into a search engine without first reading the terminal output.

concepts.failure: Passing big data between tasks via XCom instead of storing it externally and passing refe…
